newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees slower growth in palm oil output.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees slower growth in palm oil output.

text.p: Palm oil production by Indonesia and Malaysia in the Oct/Sept 1996/97 period was forecast at 13.14 million tonnes, up from 12.63 million in the same 95/96 period, the independent newsletter Oil World said on Tuesday.
But the four percent output rise in 96/97 would be down from a seven percent advance in the current season over 94/95, when production rose 10 percent from 93/94 levels.
Oil World said while the mature area in Indonesia was still growing fast, Malaysia saw increased replantings of palm area and was lacking in land and labour.
Indonesia's yield cycle -- depending on rainfall 25 months before a harvest -- had been depressed since early 1995 but would start to improve after May 1997.
In West Malaysia, yields were good until last month. They would be down in Aug-Nov 1996 and pick up again from December.
But in the country's East, a high yield period would end in January 1997 and yields should stay down at least until July.
The two Asian countries account for four-fifths of world gross exports.
